A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAPID and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The original material can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendices D–E.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, dialogue-generation evaluations, context-length analyses and retrieval-robustness tests in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds component-latency measurements and comparisons with TriForce and MInference.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 2.3–2.4 retain the same retrieval-based drafting, knowledge-transfer update, acceptance rule and residual sampling procedure. The added experiments do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate InfiniteBench, LongBench v2 and the adapted MT-Bench-101 dialogue task, including the same robustness scenarios. The new appendix comparisons use the existing LongBench v2 (Long, CoT) task; LWM-Text-Chat-128K is an additional model, not additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix E adds evaluated comparisons with TriForce and MInference in Tables 6–7, substantially broadening the acceleration approaches compared. TriForce was previously only discussed as related work. Existing LC, RAG, naive SD and MagicDec comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The added TriForce comparison uses LWM-Text-Chat-128K and specifies a 4096-token retrieval budget, chunk size 8 and draft-cache budget 256. Appendix D.2 separately measures retrieval, prefill and generation latency. Previously reported protocols in Section 3 and Appendix C remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds an efficiency analysis addressing computational cost and retrieval overhead, including a component-latency breakdown for two model sizes. Existing context-length sensitivity, retrieval-quality robustness and dialogue analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same uncertainty values for acceptance rate and throughput. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures; its new empirical tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–3 retain their results. New Table 6 reports RAPID/TriForce accuracy of 21.6/18.0 and speedup of 2.56/1.27 on LWM-Text-Chat-128K. Table 7 adds MInference results: 30.9 accuracy, 9.10-second prefill and 0.62 speedup. Table 5 adds retrieval and generation timings. These are focused additional results, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 introduces symbolic FLOPs expressions for long-context generation, RAG drafting, SD and RAPID, relating amortized cost to acceptance rates. The method equations, Proposition 2.1 and proofs in Appendices A–B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain retrieval-based speculation, inference-time knowledge transfer, self/upward speculation and improved quality with faster long-context decoding. The abstract changes emphasis toward robustness already claimed in v1's introduction; it does not materially redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion explains why retrieval overhead is small for the evaluated workload, attributes advantages over TriForce to semantic relevance rather than attention scores, and identifies MInference's prefill advantage and potential complementarity. It also explains TriForce's omission from the original model comparisons through a stated GQA compatibility constraint.

D1.justification: v2 supplies TriForce configuration details and clarifies that indexing and retrieval occur on the input context during inference. The code-access reference changes from John-AI-Lab/RAPID to NUS-TRAIL/RAPID. Existing RAPID hyperparameters, temperatures and GPU configurations remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds discussion of REST, Ouroboros and Speculative RAG. Appendix E introduces citations and positioning for MInference and the additional model, while explaining relationships to TriForce and sparse attention. The overall research positioning is retained; the additional GQA bibliography entry duplicates an already cited work.

P1.justification: v2 adds RAPID to the title, lightly rewrites the abstract, corrects SRAM to DRAM in the background, and adds acknowledgments and appendix subsections. Most existing prose and the section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds four appendix tables for FLOPs, component latency and additional comparisons, with localized text reflow. Existing figures and main table structures remain. Running headers regress from the paper title to the placeholder 'Title Suppressed Due to Excessive Size'.

improvement.justification: Appendices D–E make the efficiency evidence more assessable by quantifying previously unreported retrieval overhead and adding relevant comparisons, including MInference's prefill advantage. These focused gains outweigh the cosmetic header regression. The main method, original results and central proofs remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
